steps.text: In a skillet on medium heat cook pork, onion, green pepper, red pepper flakes, and garlic until pork is crumbly. Drain off excess fat, but leave a small amount.

Combine butter, salt, and pepper with the meat mixture and stir until butter melts. Slowly sift flour over the top. Mix gently and allow mixture to cook for 5 minutes. It will burn, so do not let it sit unguarded. Don't forget to scrape the bottom of the pan. Add the sage and thyme.

Slowly stir in milk, about a half a cup at a time, and incorporate it well. When the mixture thickens, add more milk. Do not let it boil vigorously, or it will burn. Add chicken bullion and let cook for five minutes. Again, if it thickens too much, add more milk. Adjust taste with more salt and pepper if needed.
Just before serving, add the parsley, and about a 1/4 cup more milk; the gravy will thicken quickly as it cools.

review.reviewBody:
This is absolutely awesome. I am not a sausage gravy person...white sauce and crumbled Jimmy Dean just don't turn the crank, ya know? But my family loves it so I tried this recipe.

It is out of this world. I used sage flavored sausage and dried thyme...also added a pinch of dried ginger as was suggested. I did cut the onion and pepper down significantly...i used 1/4 c red banana pepper and 1/2 c finely chopped onion...don't skip the parsley at the end...it is a nice touch.

I like the heat of the cayenne, but that is up to you. I also substituted an envelope of McCormick Sausage Gravy mix for the flour. Be prepared to add some extra milk.

I served with homemade granola, fresh fruit and yogurt (made me feel better about serving the heart attack biscuits). This is now in my brunch repertiore!
Made this with turkey sausage since we don’t eat pork. Turned out pretty tasty and my family loved it. I’ll probably cut back on the onions a bit next time.Thank you!!

I doubled this recipe because biscuits and gravy is a favorite in out home and something I once a year cook. We could definitely eat it daily or weekly but let's face it, it's a dish that isn't healthy and takes time to prepare. I also made extra gravy because we love the gravy. We have a meat market in town that carries all different flavors of sausage. I found just plain sausage and the spices the recipe calls for to bland for our tastes and it does take a bit to prepare so it got four stars from us. This time I used 1lb of Italian pork sausage and one oound of Buffalo flavored prom sausage. I threw in a few garlic cloves with onions and pinion powder and fresh ground pepper. We all added the salt and more pepper once it was plated. Doubled the gravy as well. And put this over fresh out of the oven biscuits. It was very tasty, perfect spice level and heat level and will def make again. This is a great and simple recipe just I've yourself some time to prepare. Thank you for sharing.

okay, yes it was very awesome BUT- i did lessen the pepper flakes & found it still quite spicy (good for me, not the kiddos!) also, be careful with the boulion cubes, it does NOT need two if you are using the "knorr" brand, as they are quite large. be sure to adjust salt seasoning AFTER dish is finished, bc the boulion is salty itself!! about 1/2 cup plus extra milk is necessary once all cooked. Otherwise GREAT recipe. will make over again with a few tweaks ;)

SO GOOD!!! Planned on all the kids coming over to start a new “New Years Eve” tradings, so I doubled the sausage and increased the milk and thickener, leaving the remaining ingredients as written. Definitely will make it again. New fan of biscuits and gravy!

The best gravy I've had in a longgg time. I used ground beef for the recipe (personal preference, the husband and I aren't huge pork fans) and it was delicious!!! I used half and half so I ended up adding a little bit of water to thin it out. This is my new go-to recipe for southern gravy.

Just like it says, yes! And definitely use cast iron or old brushed aluminum, but I always add a little cream sherry to any white gravy, maybe 2-3 tbls to this recipe just before done. Also, use , canned fat free milk and thin with water. Stays rich, rich, rich but "not so much" wink wink...

This is a great recipe! The first time I made it, I was short on bell peppers and a few other ingredients and it was amazing. This time I made it according to the recipe, having all the herbs required. The only thing is that I halved the red pepper. That was sufficient! I also didn't add all the bouillon this time. Had I realized how much was supposed to go in at the end, I might have eased up on the salt in the beginning. We had it over biscuits and plain white rice. I'm SO happy to have a recipe for a gravy with heaps of flavor!

This was amazing!! I adjusted a couple amounts, with peppers and onions and spices, cut them in half because they were unfamiliar to my audience and I didn't want to overwhelm them. I also used a veggie sausage substitute and a couple tablespoons of olive oil in the beginning because I don't do a lot of meat. This was the best thing I have ever put in my mouth. I may even boost back a couple spices when I make it again but this will be something I make (with leftovers) maybe weekly, maybe forever!! Thanks!

My family loved this. I followed the recipe, but doubled it. Next time (and there will be a next time) I won't add salt as I cook. The sausage (Bob Evans with sage) and the bullion cubes added enough. Better to have your guests add salt at the table if they want it. I highly recommend this for a "breakfast for dinner" night.
Be forewarned this is a spicy take on b&g but it absolutely rocked! I left out the meat and I used Anaheim instead of green pepper. I'll be making this one again

I've been making this for years now with just a few changes: I swapped out the green bell pepper for red, the bullion cubes for chicken broth or stock, and the red pepper flakes for a few dashes of hot sauce to taste. EVERYONE loves it! My oldest son is 33 and still asks me to make or for his birthday dinner!
Minor changes were made but the outcome was still fantastic....

I have never made sausage gravy before. This was so easy and delicious....husband ate 3 helpings. I didn't have fresh herbs or bell pepper so used dried seasoning, 1/2 teaspoon each of thyme and sage. I had Half & half left over from another recipe and used 2 cups of that in place of milk but did thin down the gravy with regular milk. I left out the chicken bouillon and salt based on other reviews stating it didn't need additional salt. I don't use black pepper so left it out as well. Stick to your ribs delicious! Will definately make this recipe again. I will definately be making this again
I left out the green pepper and used dried herbs. Will make this again as it turned out very good.
Everyone loves this recipe.
Wonderful! I like the extras that go into the gravy. Thank you!
Fantastic! This was the best gravy I have ever made. It went great with biscuits and over a breakfast casserole.

Excellent recipe. I skipped the bell peppers, but including the onion, garlic, and sage really boosted the savory flavor of the gravy. My primary gripe with so many country gravies is that they are too bland. This one is very much not bland.

This is my go to recipe for sausage gravy. Someone said too many spices but that's what makes it full of flavor. I'm Hungarian so we like our spice and flavor. The only change I make is ,depending on the thickness, I will substitute flour for a prepackaged gravy mix and use the sausage drippings as well. I know it's bit overkill but again I love flavor. Made with my homemade buttermilk biscuits and spicy sausage, I have yet to have anyone say that they hate my biscuits and gravy. Thank you for this recipe.
